description:
Prepare the verified stale-binary test artifact once per nextest invocation so six independent semantic tests do not occupy worker slots while serially waiting on the same nested build.

## Background

The warm profile attributes 95,249 aggregate milliseconds to the six stale-binary semantic tests. They intentionally share one verified nested Cargo build, but each process currently enters the fixture protocol and lock path independently. Move the one-time preparation into a supported nextest setup mechanism whose duration remains inside the measured nextest command, then let each semantic test independently consume the verified artifact and record its own observation. Preserve a correct fallback for direct `cargo test` execution.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A default pinned-nextest invocation prepares exactly one source- and binary-provenance-keyed stale child artifact before the six semantic tests run, and setup time remains inside the nextest wall-clock measurement.
- [hard] REQ-02: All six existing semantic test identities execute independently and retain their assertions, with evidence attributing exactly one verified nested Cargo build and five verified reuses to those identities.
- [hard] REQ-03: Direct cargo-test execution remains correct, concurrent publication is atomic and no-replace, corrupt or occupied cache entries fail closed, and no semantic test waits for a redundant nested Cargo build after successful setup.
- [hard] REQ-04: The pinned nextest configuration, setup helper self-tests, complete scratch-build target, cargo-ci self-test, formatting, and warning-free linting pass without changing the suite clock or duration threshold.

## Notes

The intended footprint is `.config/nextest.toml`, one focused setup helper under `scripts/`, and the stale-binary fixture modules under `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build`. Do not regenerate the integrated suite profile in this leaf; the parent performance issue owns combined profiling.


## Acceptance clarification

REQ-02 is evaluated according to the supported nextest setup topology: one verified nested Cargo build is truthfully attributed to the run-bound setup receipt, and all six independently named semantic identities must each record a verified prepared-artifact consumption. No test identity may be mislabeled as the builder. Direct cargo-test fallback retains its independently observable single-builder/reuse contract.
title: Prebuild the stale-binary semantic fixture inside nextest
